vo.en: You physically cannot lift this finger.

visual.description: A close-up shot of a man's hand with fingers spread, pointing directly at the camera with intensity.

vo.en: Fold your hands together like a prayer, then tuck your middle fingers inside so your knuckles touch and lock.

visual.description: Two hands coming together in a prayer position and folding the middle fingers down into the palms.

vo.en: Now, try lifting your thumbs. Easy, right? Your index fingers and pinkies move too because they have independent tendons.

visual.description: Close up of a person's thumbs and pinky fingers moving freely while the middle fingers stay folded.

vo.en: But here is the creepy part. Keep those middle fingers locked tight and try to lift both your ring fingers.

visual.description: A man's hand visibly straining to move the ring finger while the middle fingers stay pressed together.

vo.en: See? Your brain is screaming at them to move, but they won't budge. They are literally paralyzed by your own anatomy.

visual.description: Abstract visualization of glowing blue neural pathways and electric signals firing rapidly in a digital brain.

vo.en: This happens because your ring finger and middle finger are physically connected by a shared tendon called the juncturae tendinum.

visual.description: An anatomical 3D render of a human hand showing the internal tendons and bones moving.

vo.en: Subscribe for tomorrow's brain test and comment STUCK if this worked on you, which is exactly why

visual.description: A person's thumb clicking the subscribe button on a modern smartphone screen in a dark room.
